items.item_text: California Licensed Occupational Therapist (OT)
American Heart Association (AHA) or American Red Cross Basic Life Support (BLS), or UC Davis Health CPR
Two (2) years of experience as an Occupational Therapist in an acute care setting

The Occupational Therapist 2 – Per Diem is an experienced clinician who provides comprehensive occupational therapy services to patients with diverse and complex rehabilitation needs. Under the direction of the Occupational Therapy Supervisor, the therapist independently evaluates patients, develops individualized treatment plans, implements evidence-based interventions, and adjusts care based on patient progress and clinical needs.
90% -Advanced Occupational Therapy Patient Care

Working with a high degree of clinical judgment and independence, the Occupational Therapist 2 collaborates with interdisciplinary healthcare teams to support functional recovery, independence, and optimal patient outcomes. As an experienced member of the therapy team, this position also serves as a clinical resource to entry-level Occupational Therapists, supports staff orientation and education, and participates in departmental training and professional development activities.
5% - Education and Training
This per diem position provides an opportunity to contribute advanced occupational therapy expertise while supporting the evolving clinical and operational needs of the rehabilitation team.
5% - Departmental Support
Flexibility and willingness to assist other staff members with their caseloads

Professional competency in occupational therapy treatment modalities including activities of daily living and transfer training, strengthening, coordination, balance, range of motion, perceptual/cognitive skills training, wheelchair prescription, fabrication of splints and adapted devices

Professional competency in occupational therapy evaluation techniques, such as range of motion testing, muscle testing, cognitive/ perceptual testing, activities of daily living evaluation, sensory testing, and use of standardized testing of upper extremity function

Ability to meet the physical and sensory demands of patient care, including assisting with patient mobility, monitoring patient conditions and equipment, and communicating effectively with patients and staff
Ability to communicate ideas and relate well with staff and patients to work as a team member
Ability to establish and maintain good rapport with patients and their families
Ability to train family in follow-through for home therapy programs; home visiting as necessary
Ability to communicate clearly on a professional basis with physicians and work cooperatively with a variety of health care professionals
Knowledge of requirements in processing for third-party payors
Knowledge of appropriate information required for patient and supply record-keeping and ability to appropriately organize written material
Ability to clearly document progress notes, discharge plans, and other written reports as requested
Ability to effectively plan and manage workload as well as coordinate scheduling of patients in assigned areas of responsibility
Ability to verbally communicate pertinent information and knowledge of the profession for training and educating other hospital service personnel
Must possess basic computer skills
